archetype.name: Playoff Team (frontcourt-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose two bigs make it a dependable winner on offense and on the glass, but whose middling perimeter defense and thin wing group keep it a step below the true title tier.

report.headline: Mobley and Allen are carrying a good offense; the defense is unproven
report.take:
Cleveland at 4-2 looks like the team it has been for two seasons: a high-efficiency offense built around Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, with a defense that has drifted to league average. The 117.2 ORtg ranks 7th and the 121 points a game rank 2nd. Mobley ranks 3rd on the power forward tab with a 68.7 TS %, and Allen is at 69.2. That pairing is why the frontcourt grades A+ while the backcourt sits at C+ and the wings at C. The record is honest. W vs Pt Diff is 0, and the margin implies exactly the 4 wins they have, so this is not a team living on coin flips.

What produces the offense is shot quality more than volume. The eFG % of 55.3 ranks 7th and the 12.8 TOV % ranks 6th, so Cleveland rarely wastes trips, and the 37.0 3P % sits above the league. The backcourt is the soft spot. Donovan Mitchell is efficient (62.4 TS %, 8th on his tab), but James Harden is at a 54.9 TS % with a -3.1 BPM and a -14.3 On-Off. Peyton Watson, effectively the entire wing group, is at 46.2 TS % and is now day-to-day. Jaylon Tyson is out, so the perimeter rotation is getting thinner, not deeper.

The numbers hide a defense that is better at the rim than the 16th-ranked DRtg suggests, and worse everywhere else. Opponents shoot 61.3% at the rim, 4th best, which is Allen and Mobley at work. But teams are getting there constantly: the Opp Rim Rate of 34.0 ranks 26th. Cleveland also forces few turnovers, with an Opp TOV % of 12.3, 25th. Opposing centers have been the clearest leak. They are scoring well over their own averages, and no team has allowed more threes to the position, which points to bigs being pulled away from the rim and left open outside.

History says this is roughly who they are. Last year's team won 52 with a 6th-ranked offense and a 15th-ranked defense, an almost identical profile. The 64-win version two seasons ago paired the league's best offense with a top-10 defense. Six games is far too few to say which way this goes. The early shape matches last season more than the 64-win year: elite bigs, a good offense, and a defense that needs the guards to hold the point of attack.

strengths.title: Two hyper-efficient bigs
strengths.body: Mobley (68.7 TS %) and Allen (69.2 TS %) are finishing nearly everything, and both rank in the top ten on their position tabs. That is the main reason the frontcourt grades A+. It is also why Cleveland outrebounds teams, ranking 4th in RPG and 7th in REB %. The exact percentages will cool off, but both players posted similar profiles in past seasons, so the strength itself is durable.

strengths.title: Clean, efficient half-court offense
strengths.body: An eFG % that ranks 7th and a TOV % that ranks 6th give Cleveland a 117.2 ORtg, well above the league. Offenses in the 116-122 range have been the norm here for three straight seasons, so this is a known baseline rather than a hot start.

strengths.title: Rim protection at the finish
strengths.body: Opponents who reach the rim convert at only 61.3%, 4th in the league and below the league mark. With Allen and Mobley on the floor that number should hold. The problem, covered below, is how often opponents get there.

concerns.title: Porous perimeter, few forced turnovers
concerns.body: Opponents take a high share of their shots at the rim (an Opp Rim Rate ranked 26th), and Cleveland forces turnovers at a rate ranked 25th. The result is a 16th-ranked DRtg despite the shot-blocking behind it. Last season's defense ranked 15th, so this looks structural rather than a slow start.

concerns.title: Harden and Watson dragging lineups
concerns.body: Harden's -3.1 BPM and -14.3 On-Off, and Watson's 46.2 TS % with a -24.2 On-Off, mark the two weakest heavy-minute pieces. Six games of On-Off is noisy; Mobley's is also negative. Still, the wing group has 0 Win Shares, and with Watson day-to-day and Tyson out there is little cover.

concerns.title: Stretch centers are torching them
concerns.body: Opposing centers are scoring and rebounding well above their own averages against Cleveland, and no team has allowed more threes to the position. It suggests Allen is being dragged out of the paint. Over six games this could be a matchup quirk, but it is the spot opponents will test.

trend.note: After an opening loss at Philadelphia they went 4-1 over the last five, scoring 124 a game and lifting the margin above the season mark, capped by a 136-111 win at Milwaukee.

weekAhead.headline: Four home games, but a Philadelphia rematch is the real test
weekAhead.body:
Five games, four in Cleveland, starting with a home-and-away pair against Oklahoma City. The Thunder are 4-2 but with a slightly negative Net Rtg, a 23rd-ranked offense and a 2nd-ranked Opp Rim FG %. That rim number makes this a direct test of whether Mobley and Allen can keep finishing. OKC's frontcourt grades D, and it has held centers well below their averages, so the Allen matchup cuts both ways. New York (2-4) owns the league's best DRB %, so second chances will be scarce. Charlotte has the league's worst ORtg, at 103.1.

The swing game is Philadelphia at home. The 76ers are 6-1 with the 2nd-best DRtg and already beat Cleveland 114-106. They are also the worst rebounding team in the league by REB % and ORB %, which is exactly where Cleveland's bigs can tilt a game. Anything at 4-1 or better would confirm the early read; 3-2 would be par.

keyMatchups.title: Bigs vs OKC's rim protection
keyMatchups.body: Oklahoma City allows only 58.2% at the rim and keeps opponents away from it, while holding centers far under their averages. Cleveland's offense runs through the efficiency of Mobley and Allen inside. Two games in three days will show whether that efficiency holds up against a good rim defense.

keyMatchups.title: Glass edge over Philadelphia
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia ranks 30th in REB % and ORB %, while Cleveland ranks 4th in RPG. Against a defense ranked 3rd that will deny clean looks, extra possessions off the boards may decide the rematch.

keyMatchups.title: Charlotte's broken offense
keyMatchups.body: The Hornets rank last in ORtg and TS % and take half their shots from three while hitting under 30%. Cleveland's perimeter defense is ordinary, but this is the week's most forgiving opponent.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Watson returns, and who soaks up wing minutes if he doesn't. The wing group is already the roster's weakest.

restOfSeason.body:
The margin and the record agree, the offense has a multi-year track record, and the frontcourt is elite. That supports a pace in the low-to-mid 50s rather than the 55 the raw six-game rate implies. The scoring will settle as the bigs' near-70% TS % cools and the schedule toughens. The ceiling depends on the defense. Last year's 15th-ranked unit produced 52 wins and a 4.1 Net Rtg. The 64-win season needed a top-10 defense alongside the best offense.

Expect a Net Rtg in the mid-single digits and a top-four seed fight with Detroit in the Central. The real lever is the perimeter: better shooting from Harden and a healthy wing rotation would add wins. More stretch-big leaks and few forced turnovers would cap this as a good, not great, team.
swingFactors: Containing dribble penetration and stretch centers

confidence.note: Six games; On-Off and shooting splits are very noisy, though history anchors the profile.
